premise: I used my late husband’s $95,000 life insurance to pay for my nephew’s $92,000 MBA after he signed a contract guaranteeing me a lifetime of free portfolio management, but when he landed a $250,000‑a‑year job he blew me off, calling it a gift; I sued for promissory estoppel, won a $340,000 judgment, and now garnish his salary to fund ‘Portfolio of Promises’ — a free financial clinic where every client sips from a mug that says ‘My MBA was funded by my aunt’s sacrifice’ while he is forced to volunteer quarterly in a tie embroidered ‘Fiduciary Fraudster.’
